images.caption: Figure 1:Overview of proposed BLIP-Live framework.We unify data, metrics, harness, and training around a shared formulation of proactivity aseffective causal response decisionsbalancing the two competing objectives of responding vs silence in the proactive streaming task.

Figure 3:Inference Harness.At each streaming timesteptt, the harness constructs an input from a system prompt (task and output schema), a rolling past-frame window, and memory of user queries and prior responses. A frozen offline VLM is queried at the target frame rate; structured output is parsed into either silence or a response attt, and accepted responses are updated into memory.

Figure A.1:Automated Harness Tuning.We plot all 100 evaluations on our BLIP-Live-780K validation with various harness design candidates for Gemma4-A4B model.
The selected models for each round are highlights (blue).
The full tuning process achieves a gain of 12.85 PAUC-F points on the validation data.

Figure A.2:Dataset review interface.Reviewers inspect each sampled video frame against the instruction and existing annotation, navigate temporally, and mark only frames requiring correction. The interface records missing responses, hallucinations, temporal boundary cases, and deletion decisions while automatically treating unmarked frames as correct.

Figure A.3:Human rating interface for PAUC-F.Raters inspect the video, ground-truth response regions, and timestamped responses from two anonymized system variants, then select the preferred response stream. The aligned timeline and side-by-side response lists expose differences in event coverage, response timing, and repetitive firing behavior.
